name: The Ghast chain
text: Ghast hang their children on a chain. Not the children, the links: one for every birth, off a crag on the Upper Dales, seven hundred years of it. Their smith'll close one for anybody who brings him a bar of iron and says their name over it. Bring good iron.
variants: There's a gap near the top of the Kinchain the Ghast won't talk about. A link sawn out, they say, by the man whose name was on it.

name: The Oskel kite
text: Watch the Oskel kite over the west moor. High and steady, all's quiet. Low and dipping, riders out. And lately the kite-wife flies the night kite every night, and she's been asking people what stands on the Upper Dales.
variants: Runa ko-Oskel says her lantern-kite showed her a thing twenty men high on the Dales, with lights going up and down it.

name: The empty row
text: Every clan keeps its bees at the Bee-Bole Crag, a row apiece. Except the top row. Put a swarm in the top row and it's gone by morning, every time. Old Bannoch says it was cut for the Bone Clan, and bees won't stay with a clan nobody says.
variants: Don't take comb from the bee-boles without paying. It's guest-honey. The clans remember a thief at the boles longer than one in a house.

name: The husher's tooth
text: Wat Hobb's sitting by his hushing-dam on the fell and won't pull it. Last time he let the water go it dug up a giant's tooth as big as a cart wheel, and Brindle said that was the hill telling him to stop. The pond's full again.
variants: They say the next hush at the Scour will turn up the rest of the giant. Wat says that's the point.

name: The black-rent
text: Nobody pays black-rent. That's what they'll tell you, every farm below the passes. Then go and look at the tally-sticks round the Pillar on the Rudd road, a stick a farm a year, hundreds of them. Isbel ko-Rudd's sat down by it with this year's and won't send it up.
variants: The riders who empty the basket on the Pillar come from Corbie Stack, they say, the old Rudd needle on the high moor. Somebody's living on it again.

name: The Bucket-Line
text: Grett ko-Brindle's strung a cable across the dale below Ghaleld and hung buckets on it, and pays twelve marks to anybody who'll walk her wheel. Hard on the legs. Honest money, though, and you can see the whole dale from the trestle.
variants: The reivers cut the Bucket-Line in the spring because Grett wouldn't pay their rent. She mended it in a month and keeps a crossbow by the wheel.

name: The Breath-Ledge
text: The Skarl don't bury their dead. They hang them in coffins on pegs up a white scar in the east fells, as high as the ropes go, so the Breath takes them first. A coffin that falls, the Breath didn't want. One fell in the big wind last winter.
variants: Mags ko-Skarl hangs the Skarl dead, and there's a peg near the top of the Breath-Ledge she's kept empty for herself.

name: The Answering Wall
text: Every clan child gets stood on the speaking-stone at the Answering Wall once and told to say their name, and the wall says it back. At dusk, the callers say, it sometimes says a name back that nobody gave it, and that's somebody being forgotten too fast.
variants: Stand on the step at the Answering Wall and call your name. It comes back off the rock like a crowd of people who all know you.

name: Smoke on Corbie Stack
text: There's smoke on Corbie Stack again, the Rudd needle on the high moor. Forty years nothing lived on it but crows. Now there's a black rag flying from the top and riders going out at night, and a door cut in the foot of it.
variants: Annet Blackrent keeps a book of every farm that pays her and every farm that doesn't. She's never burned a farm that paid, they say. They say it like it's a kindness.

name: The thing on the Dales
text: The thralls have been carrying bone up the Upper Dales all year, and now there's something standing up there in a cage of poles, twenty men high, and the hags going up and down it on ladders. A bone-warden's counting it. He says it's three bones short.
variants: A thrall's what a bone remembers of walking, the hags say. Nobody wants to know what a whole giant remembers.
